title: Spool item sidecar
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.1 and 4.6, #773), not implemented. The JSON file that completes one item of the capture spool: `items/<seq, 12 digits>-<id>.json`, written by `sizeup-radio` under tmp/ and renamed into items/ LAST, after the item's audio. A reader lists `*.json` only. `kind` says what the item is: `segment` (a finished FM, paging or airband transmission), `call` (a finished P25 call) or `metrics` (one minute of signal records, no audio); a reader acknowledges and skips a kind it does not know. Wall-clock times are Unix seconds with a fraction (never milliseconds); a name ending in `_boot` is seconds on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, comparable only while `boot` is the reader's own boot id. The layout and the rules a spool directory must keep are in contracts/capture/spool.md; tests/contracts_capture.py `check_spool` is their reference check.

v.description: The sidecar's version, 1. A change that only adds optional keys keeps it.

kind.description: What the item is. An unknown kind is acknowledged and skipped by the reader.

id.description: The item's idempotency id; the reader drops an id it already handled. A segment: today's clip id, `<channel label without spaces>-<int(start * 1000)>`. A call: trunk-recorder's file stem. A metrics item: `metrics-<int(minute start * 1000)>`. It matches CLIP_ID (sizeup/app.py) and has no `..`. The same transmission never gets two ids.

seq.description: The item's sequence number: one counter for the whole spool, taken under the publish lock. Per channel it rises in the order the transmissions ended; nothing is promised across channels. 12 decimal digits at most (the file name's width).

spool_epoch.description: The spool this item belongs to: the 16 hex characters of the spool's EPOCH file. A reader whose cursor names another epoch starts from 0.

published.description: When the sidecar was renamed into items/, Unix seconds (wall clock).

published_boot.description: The same moment on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, seconds since boot.

boot.description: The boot id `closed_boot` and `published_boot` belong to: the kernel's (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id), or where there is none (macOS) an id made at process start. Opaque: compared for equality only.

capture.title: The writer
capture.description: Which capture wrote the item, for the compare tool.

impl.description: The implementation: `python`, or a native daemon's name.

contract.description: The capture contract's major version the writer speaks, 1.

channel.title: The channel
channel.description: The channel the transmission was heard on (a segment).

label.description: The channel's label, as in the wish.

mhz.description: The frequency as heard, MHz, to 4 decimals. Airband: the frequency of this transmission (#260).

sdr.description: The serial of the dongle that received it.

start.description: When the transmission started, Unix seconds: the wall clock (CLOCK_REALTIME), stamped by the squelch from frame arrival. A call: the call's start as trunk-recorder gives it.

end.description: When it ended, Unix seconds (wall clock).

closed_boot.description: CLOCK_BOOTTIME at the squelch's close, seconds since boot (a call: when capture's ingest took the finished call). What `late` is measured from, while `boot` is the reader's boot.

replayed.description: A P25 call capture took from its replay mark after its own restart (#753). Informative: lateness is decided by age alone.

reason.description: Why the transmission ended, as `Segment.reason`. Open: a reader takes any text.

partial.description: Cut by something other than the transmission ending (`stall`, `stopped`, `rtl_fm ended`).

cont.description: Paging (#61): opened within the continuation window of the transmission before it.

hold_until.description: Paging (#61): the wall-clock time until which the squelch watches for a continuation, Unix seconds; 0 for none.

breaks.description: Paging (#61): each drop the long hang held through, as [start, end] in seconds into the audio; [] for none.

keyup.title: Key-up link
keyup.description: Set on a piece cut from a longer recording at a key-up (#645); null for a transmission that was not cut. The ids are the pieces' own item ids (`<label without spaces>-<int(start * 1000)>`).

split.description: Why this piece was cut from the one before it: `gap`, `id` or `level`; "" for the first piece.

first_start.description: The start of the recording's first piece, Unix seconds (the first piece: its own `start`).

prev_start.description: The start of the piece before this one, Unix seconds; null for the first piece.

parent.description: The item id of the recording's first piece (the first piece: its own id).

prev.description: The item id of the piece before this one; "" for the first piece.

levels.title: Signal levels
levels.description: What the squelch measured for this transmission. An FM channel sends the FM keys, an AM (airband) channel the AM keys; `quieting_db` is on both with its own meaning.

quieting_db.description: FM: how far the carrier quieted the hiss, dB. AM: the carrier over the floor, dB.

q_open.description: FM: quieting over the first 0.3 s of carrier, dB; null when not measured.

q_close.description: FM: quieting over the last 0.3 s of carrier, dB; null when not measured.

hiss_db.description: FM: the idle hiss level the quieting was measured against, relative dB; null when not measured.

floor_db.description: FM: a background carrier's quieting, dB; null when there was none.

floor_dbfs.description: AM: the noise floor the carrier was measured against, dBFS.

snr_db.description: AM: the audio's signal over noise, dB.

opened.description: AM: how the squelch opened: `carrier` (a carrier over the threshold) or `sustained` (a weaker one that held).

preroll_s.description: AM: audio kept from before the squelch opened, seconds.

notched_hz.description: AM: the steady tones notched out of the audio, each a frequency in Hz; [] for none.

speech_s.description: Seconds of speech in the audio (`fm.speech_seconds`).

ids.description: The radio ids of the transmission, in today's merge order: the live tap's first, then the segment's own; [] for none.

id_burst_seen.description: A data burst was there, in the key-up window or at either edge, decoded or not (#163).

mdc_crc_failed.description: MDC-1200 sync hits whose CRC failed, a count.

bursts.description: Data bursts cut off the transmission's edges, a count.

alarm_key.description: The `key` of the urgent alarm capture raised for this carrier (capture-urgent-item.schema.json); "" for none.

tones_live.description: Paging: the tone pairs the live decode showed, without names. Informative: the page's own tone decode runs over the audio.

items.title: One tone pair, live
items.description: A pair as the live decode showed it.

at.description: When the pair was certain, Unix seconds.

audio_dropped.description: The audio was removed at a bound (age, size, the free-space reserve) and `audio` is null for that reason. Never set on an item with an emergency id.

bursts_audio.description: The file name in items/ of the cut-off id bursts, `<seq, 12 digits>-<id>.mdc.wav`; null for none.

system.description: A call: trunk-recorder's short name of the P25 system.

freq_hz.description: A call: its voice channel, Hz; null when unknown.

signal_db.description: A call: the signal trunk-recorder measured, dB; null when it measured none.

noise_db.description: A call: the noise trunk-recorder measured, dB; null when it measured none.

emergency.description: A call: the call's JSON says it was granted as an emergency call.

encrypted.description: A call: the call's JSON says it was encrypted.

turns.description: A call: its key-ups in order, after the live grants were applied.

grants_applied.description: A call: the live grants changed a turn (`apply_grants` returned true). Never true on a replayed call.

tr.description: A call: the file name in items/ of trunk-recorder's own JSON for the call, a hard link, `<seq, 12 digits>-<id>.tr`. It does not end in `.json`: in items/ only a sidecar does.

records.description: A metrics item: the `floor` and `cc` records of sizeup/cloud/metrics.py as they are today, one object each, with `k` (the record's kind), `s` (its subject) and `at` (Unix seconds).

radio-id.title: One radio id
radio-id.description: A radio id decoded from an MDC-1200 or FleetSync packet.

id.description: The radio's id as decoded, digits as a string.

system.description: The signalling it was sent in. A reader takes a word it does not know as an id of an unknown system.

emergency.description: The packet was an emergency (the radio's emergency button).

from.description: Where it was decoded: `live` by the live tap at the key-up, `lookback` by the tap's look back over the carrier's first frames, `burst` from a data burst cut off the transmission's edge, `audio` from the whole-clip decode at the close.

audio.title: The item's audio file
audio.description: The audio of the transmission, beside the sidecar in items/. null when there is none: the wish says the channel is not recorded, or the audio was dropped at a bound (`audio_dropped`).

file.description: The file's name in items/: `<seq, 12 digits>-<id>.wav`. A name only, never a path.

encoding.description: The sample format. `s16le`: signed 16-bit little-endian PCM. For a segment it is the float audio clipped to +-1 and scaled by 32767, exactly today's `<id>.src.wav`.

rate_hz.description: Samples per second, Hz. 16000 for a segment; trunk-recorder's own rate for a call (the reader resamples).

samples.description: Samples per channel in the file, a count.

bytes.description: The whole file's size, bytes. A file on disk of another size (short or empty after a power cut) is logged and skipped, never parsed as audio. A segment's file is a 44-byte header and the samples: 44 + 2 x samples.

turn.title: One key-up inside a P25 call
turn.description: One talker's turn, after the live grants were applied (`apply_grants`).

src.description: The P25 radio id, digits as a string; "" when none was decoded.

pos_s.description: Where the turn starts in the call's audio, seconds.

len_s.description: The turn's length, seconds of audio; null: until the next turn.

time.description: The turn's start, Unix seconds (estimated: trunk-recorder gives whole seconds); null when unknown.

emergency.description: The call's JSON flags this key-up as an emergency (`srcList[].emergency`).

errors.description: The voice channel's error count for the turn (`freqList[].error_count`).

via.description: How the turn got its talker: `srclist` (the call's own list), `grant` (named by a live grant), `freqlist`. Today's code also says `split` (cut at a grant) and never `freqlist`: see contracts/README.md, Capture split.
